Aggregate a CWP dataset to a coarser time and space resolution

Source: R/cwp_aggregate.R
cwp_aggregate.Rd

Sums a dataset in CWP format by year (or month) and by 5 degree square (the 1 degree squares are grouped into their 5 degree square), keeping all its other dimensions. The result is much smaller than the dataset and keeps its totals: it can be stored, and compared with the aggregate of another version of the dataset (see cwp_split_common_periods() and comprehensive_cwp_dataframe_analysis()).

Usage

cwp_aggregate(
  data,
  time_resolution = c("year", "month"),
  spatial_resolution = 5,
  dimensions = c("source_authority", "species", "gear_type", "fishing_fleet",
    "fishing_mode", "geographic_identifier", "measurement_type", "measurement_unit")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in CWP format: time_start (or year), measurement_value and dimension columns.

time_resolution

"year" or "month": period of time_start in the result.

spatial_resolution

5 to group the 1 degree squares into their 5 degree square, NULL to keep the geographic identifiers as they are. Codes that are not 1 degree squares are always kept.

dimensions

Dimension columns to keep (those absent from data are ignored).

Value

A data.table with time_start (first day of the period, as a string), the dimensions, measurement_value (sum) and n_rows (number of rows of data summed).

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  source_authority = "IOTC", species = "YFT", gear_type = "01.1",
  time_start = c("2020-01-01", "2020-02-01"),
  geographic_identifier = c("5100050", "5101051"),
  measurement_unit = "t", measurement_value = c(1, 2)
)
cwp_aggregate(d)
#>    time_start source_authority species gear_type geographic_identifier
#>        <char>           <char>  <char>    <char>                <char>
#> 1: 2020-01-01             IOTC     YFT      01.1               6100050
#>    measurement_unit measurement_value n_rows
#>              <char>             <num>  <int>
#> 1:                t                 3      2
